main: On 102,561 test CVEs (294 exploited), **gradient boosting catches 33.7% [28–39] of exploited CVEs at 110 patches a month**, against **25.2% [20–30] for the best day-0 rule** (+8.5 points [+1.7, +15.3], P(better) 99%) and **18.6% for today's CVSS ranking** (+15.1 [+8.8, +21.5]). At K = 305: 49.3% vs 42.2% and 36.1%. Against **EPSS with lookahead (29.6%) the lead is +4.1 points [−2.7, +10.5], P 86%: ahead, but not clearly**. EPSS has the higher PR-AUC (0.069 vs 0.053), which is driven by its top ranks. Like-for-like, EPSS with day-0 scores only catches 5.1%, because 70% of CVEs have no EPSS score until the day after publication. Late fusion (29.3%) is 4.3 points behind the headline [−1.0, +9.1]. All test numbers are below validation (headline 47.1% on val).
own: Today's rule, **CVSS ≥ 9 (CNA), now flags 385 CVEs a month** on test (196 on val, 110 on train) and catches **41.2%**. Gradient boosting with the same 385 patches catches **51.7%** (fusion 55.4%), about **+10 points for the same work**. Against 'phrase OR CVSS ≥ 9' (387/month, 47.3%) the gain is +4.4 points. Against the generous fallback rule (516/month, 44.9%) it is +11.6 points (56.5%).
curve: Gradient boosting beats both day-0 rules at every capacity from 10 to 1,000 patches a month (e.g. 21.1 vs 18.5 at 50; 73.1 vs 66.8 at 1,000). **EPSS (with lookahead) leads only at very small K**: 16.3 vs 12.2 at 10/month and 22.4 vs 21.1 at 50. That is EPSS's high PR-AUC, which comes from its very top ranks. **From about 80 patches a month the model leads, and the gap widens with K**: +4.1 at 110, +3.9 at 305, +9.2 at 1,000. Late fusion overtakes gradient boosting above ~350/month (60.9 vs 55.8 at 500), which matches its stronger @305 on dev.
epss: Only **29.9% of test CVEs have an EPSS score on publication day** (62 of 294 exploited); 69.5% get their first score the next day, and 9 CVEs get none within 7 days. So 'EPSS by day 1' ≈ 'EPSS within 7 days' (29.6% both), while 'day-0 only' is 5.1%. **During EPSS v3** (to 2025-03-17, 44 exploited) the headline scores 43.2% vs EPSS 40.9%. **During v4** (250 exploited) it scores 32.8% vs 30.8%. The gap is similar under both EPSS versions.
nyk: **109 of the 294 exploited test CVEs (37%) were already in KEV when EPSS produced the score used.** On the remaining 185, **EPSS falls from 29.6% to 14.6% [9–20]**, while **gradient boosting keeps 30.4% [24–37]** and the best rule 29.4%. That makes the headline ~2x EPSS on the CVEs where the label can't have leaked into EPSS. The same pattern held on val (EPSS 10.0% vs headline 52.5%, pre-test). With the day-0 cut only 14 CVEs drop (280 kept): headline 34.2%, EPSS day-0 4.3%. This rests on the stated assumption that EPSS uses KEV. Even without that assumption, a score dated after the KEV listing isn't something a team has on day 0.
robust: **Walk-forward 2022-24 → 2025 (test year 2025): 41.9% [34–50]**, in line with gradient boosting's dev periods (WF 2023 39.7, WF 2024-H1 55.6, val 47.1). **2026 (Jan–Aug): 23.9% [17–32]**. By quarter the headline holds 37.8–45.7% from 2025Q1 to 2026Q1, then drops to **25.3% in 2026Q2 and 7.7% in 2026Q3** (Jul 1–Aug 20; 39 exploited). Late fusion collapses further (5.4% and 0.0%). The text-MLP seeds are stable (fusion 28.2–29.9% per seed vs 29.3% ensemble). The uncertain-phrase check was N/A on test (0 uncertain rows).
calibration: Out of sample, the calibrated probability is only modestly better than a constant: **Brier 0.002816 vs 0.002858**, log loss 0.0169 vs 0.0196. It **over-predicts on average (0.42% predicted vs 0.29% observed)**, because the base rate fell from 0.34% (dev) to 0.29%. In the **top 0.5% of scores it under-predicts: 4.4% predicted vs 7.6% observed**. Ranking is what the model is used for; the probability is a rough guide and should be recalibrated when the model is retrained.
drift_year: **Not everyone drops.** At fixed K = 110, gradient boosting falls 41.9 → 23.9, fusion 39.1 → 17.8 and the best rule 29.5 → 20.0. CVSS ranking is flat (19.2 → 17.8) and **EPSS is flat (29.6 → 29.6)**. **Volume is a large part of it**: CVEs per month went 2,607 (dev) → 4,013 (2025) → 6,801 (2026), so K = 110 covers 4.2% → 2.7% → 1.6% of a month. At a **constant share** (4.2% of each month, = 110 in a dev month), the headline goes 49.7 → 34.1: the drop shrinks but remains (−15.6 points vs −18.0). EPSS stays at 39, and CVSS ranking actually *improves* (23.4 → 29.1). So there is also a genuine model-specific decline in 2026.
drift_mix: **The exploited CVEs did not come from unseen vendors**: 88.9% of 2026's exploited CVEs have a vendor seen in dev (83.6% in 2025), and 70.4% are from vendors with earlier KEV entries (68.6%). What changed is **the competition for slots**. CVEs per month from vendors with KEV history went 696 (dev) → 1,246 (2025) → **2,376 (2026)**, and CNA CVSS ≥ 9 went 124 → 238 → **606 a month**. The model's strongest signal (vendor KEV history) now marks thousands of CVEs a month. Its catch rate for exploited CVEs from KEV vendors fell from 53.2% to 31.6%. Microsoft shows it: 16 of 28 caught in 2025, **5 of 23** in 2026. Exploitation phrases at publication also became rarer (11.3% → 3.7% of exploited CVEs), removing a strong signal. Meanwhile 46.7% of 2026's exploited CVEs had CNA CVSS ≥ 9 (36.5% in 2025), which is why CVSS ranking held up.
rolling: **Over the whole test period, retraining every quarter is a wash: 34.7% [29–40] vs 33.7% for the frozen model (+1.0 [−3.3, +5.6])**. The timing matters, though. In 2025 retraining **hurt slightly** (−4.4 [−9.7, +0.7]; 2025Q3 −13.9), because the newest 2025 data added noise. In **2026 it helped: +7.4 [+0.0, +15.2] (31.3% vs 23.9%)**. In 2026Q2 that was +12.2 [+3.1, +22.4] (37.5% vs 25.3%), and 2026Q3 was 17.9% vs 7.7%. 2025Q2 is identical by construction (the rolling model trains on exactly dev), which confirms the simulation. The 90-day label delay means a retrain always lags at least a quarter behind. **For the CISO: retraining is cheap insurance against drift, not a performance boost in stable periods**. Retraining **plus re-checking K against monthly volume** matters more: K = 110 is a shrinking share of a growing CVE stream.
final: **Gradient boosting (the pre-registered headline) is the best day-0 method on test: 33.7% at 110 patches a month vs 25.2% for the best rule and 18.6% for today's CVSS ranking. At the CVSS ≥ 9 rule's own 385 patches it catches 51.7% vs 41.2%.** It is level-to-ahead of EPSS overall (29.6%; +4.1, not significant). On exploited CVEs not yet in KEV when EPSS scored them, it is about twice EPSS (30.4% vs 14.6%). Performance fell from 47.1% (val) and 41.9% (2025) to 23.9% in 2026. Exploratory analysis attributes this mainly to volume growth against a fixed K and to more CVEs from KEV-history vendors competing for the slots. Quarterly retraining recovers part of the 2026 loss (31.3%).
